maria: Heads-up: replay harness results disagree with synthetic load for the same model/seq distribution. Replay shows 30% higher p95 and lower KV hit-rate. Anyone seen this before?
kevin: Not great. Are you replaying real traffic (same client IDs, same prefix lengths)?
maria: Yes — exact client traces from last week. I ran 1h replay against dedicated pool A (g4dn-like). Benchmarks: 1000 rps nominal, 8–16 token completions, prefix reuse ~45%.
jordan: Synthetic run uses uniform seq lengths and warm KV prime, right? That usually inflates cache hits.
maria: Correct. Synthetic was uniform [12] length and we prefilled KV cache with a `warm_kv()` pass. Replay doesn't prefill (we wanted realism).
tess: Can you paste perf profile? curious where kernel selection or batching spikes.
maria: Pasted below (trimmed):
```
[PROFILE] total_requests:3600
avg_latency: 42ms
p50: 30ms p95: 120ms p99: 220ms
kernel_select_ms: avg 4.1ms -> when cold 13.4ms
batching_wait_ms: avg 6.5ms
kv_lookup_ms: avg 0.9ms, hit_rate: 46%
KV-miss extra tokens: +18%
```
kevin: kernel_select jumping to 13ms during cold windows is suspicious — maybe the quantized-kernel path falls back to a slower kernel when sequence length changes. Did you log kernel versions?
maria: bench-bot attached a log snippet: `kernel=v2_int8_fast` then `kernel=v2_generic_fallback` when we hit low occupancy.
bench-bot: /attach logs: kernel_switch events for 1780509876 replay run: 78 switches over 1h, correlated with scale events.
jordan: That matches autoscale spikes. When a new worker boots we see non-optimized kernels until JIT/cache warms. That would bump kernel_select and batch formation time.
tess: Also KV cache miss rate at 46% is low. Replay includes diverse user prefixes; synthetic warm run was ~88% hit. That explains throughput drop.
kevin: For apples-to-apples we should: (1) use same prefix distribution, (2) run synthetic with "no prefill" mode, (3) simulate scale events in both harnesses.
maria: Agreed. I propose a 3x experiment: A) Replay (no prefill), B) Synthetic (no prefill, same prefix histogram), C) Synthetic(warm) as control. Each run 30m, ramp 0->1k rps, then hold. Capture kernel_switch, kv_hits, batch_sizes, gpu_util, start_time->ready_time for new workers.
jordan: Add worker cold-start metric: time from instance launch to first optimized kernel compile. Tag it `kernel_ready_ms`.
tess: Also capture burst-credit consumption and dedicated pool buffer occupancy. I saw one case where burst credits dipped and autoscaler refused new workers until credits recovered — weird policy. @srebot can you check policy?
srebot: Autoscale policy: burst_credits are consumed when adding non-reserved workers. There is a 60s cooldown and a soft limit at 80% credits. Behavior is by design but can cause delayed scaling if sustained bursts occur.
kevin: That's the policy, but if kernel_ready_ms is >> scale_up_ms, user-visible latency spikes. We should measure interplay: scale_up_ms, kernel_ready_ms, prefix_reuse_ratio.
maria: Running a short proof run now with instrumentation flags: `--emit kernel_switch,kvcache,scale_event --no-kv-prefill`
bench-bot: Quick live summary after 10m: p95 145ms, kv_hit 49%, kernel_ready_ms median 900ms but 95th 4.2s, scale_up_ms median 2.1s.
jordan: 4.2s kernel_ready tail is killer. Probably due to on-first-request compiler + loading specialized kernels into GPU L2. We should consider keeping a tiny warm pool of one extra worker per zone that stays idle but kernel-ready.
tess: Or pre-jit kernels on boot (defer traffic until kernel_ready). But that adds cold capacity cost. Tradeoff: cost vs tail latency. Let's quantify cost of 1 warm standby vs 5s p95 reduction.
kevin: Also tweak batching heuristics: when KV hit-rate low, prefer smaller batch sizes to reduce wasted token compute. Maybe dynamic batch cap based on recent kv_hit_rate.
maria: Action items: 1) Run A/B with 3 configs (replay, synthetic-matched-no-prefill, synthetic-warm) — collect kernel_switch, kernel_ready_ms, scale_up_ms, kv_hit, batch_size_histogram, p95. 2) Add bench harness flag to replay that can optionally prefill KV with same per-client prefix distribution to test sensitivity. 3) Run two dedicated pools: one with 1 warm standby per AZ. 4) Evaluate cost delta and p95 improvements.
jordan: I'll add a dashboard panel for `kernel_ready_ms` and `kernel_switch_rate`.
tess: I'll open a short RFC for standby-worker tradeoffs. Include a cost model for reserved vs standby.
kevin: For immediate mitigation, we can change autoscaler to wait 1st optimized kernel_ready before routing traffic to new worker (traffic held for <X ms). Might flatten tail. But we need to measure start-to-service latency if traffic queued.
maria: Thanks team. I'll kick off the experiments and post raw logs here. If anyone wants to tag into the runs: test id 17805-kvspin-1.
bench-bot: test artifacts: s3://bench-results/17805-kvspin-1/ (logs, profiles, trace.jsonl) :thumbsup:
kevin: Great. One more note: ensure apples-to-apples CPU/GPU kernel builds — don't mix debug vs release kernels in runs. Last time we accidentally had debug kernels on a staging image and saw 2x kernel_select.
maria: Noted. Using release build image `redwood/runtime:v2026.03`.
tess: Nice. Ping when experiments complete, we can triage mitigation in next oncall window. :rocket:
